To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the resistance to apoptosis of Pirc rats is not mirrored by a significant modulation of the expression of genes involved in genotoxic stress response.

the expression of genes involved in DNA repair and antioxidant response, which were induced by cytotoxic insult, is not sufficient to explain the resistance to apoptosis observed in Apc-mutant Pirc rats, suggesting the involvement of additional pathways.
the expression of genes related to the response to DNA damage was increased in the mucosa of wt and PIRC rats after DMH treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of gene expression profile of the colon mucosa in wt and Pirc Rats after cytotoxic insult.

the study of the gene expression profile in colon mucosa after a cytotoxic insult in wt and Pirc rat, spontaneously developing intestinal neoplasia, and the possible relationship with resistance to apoptosis during carcinogenesis.
a possible role for interferon-induced genes in the resistance to apoptosis during colon carcinogenesis in Apc-mutant rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Pirc rats are not resistant to DMH-induced colon apoptosis but are less sensitive to the apoptotic effect of DMH.
the resistance to apoptosis in Apc-mut Pirc rat is not due to a defective induction of the genes involved in apoptosis and oxidative stress response.
the resistance of Pirc rats to DMH-induced colon apoptosis is not related to the differential gene expression of these genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the early phase of carcinogenesis, Apc mutation is associated to a lower antioxidant capacity, which could be responsible for the higher resistance to apoptosis of Pirc rats.
the Pirc rat model may be useful in the study of early events in the colon carcinogenesis, but the resistance to apoptosis in this model is not due to major changes in gene expression.

, despite a blunter induction of apoptosis in DMH-treated Apc-mut Pirc rats, the whole gene expression profile in the colonic mucosa is not different from that observed in DMH-treated wild type (wt) Pirc rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in Pirc rats, the resistance to apoptosis after DMH is probably not related to a specific gene modulation, but it is likely to depend on a more complex mechanism.
the Pirc rat model of resistance to apoptosis during carcinogenesis could be a valuable model for understanding the molecular basis of the resistance to apoptosis in human colon cancer.
the resistance to apoptosis in Pirc colon mucosa is not associated with an altered gene expression of stress-response genes.
